native_result.query: What is the average length of original papers in Experimental Economics and that in Psychology?
native_result.HypoA: Studies in Experimental Economics tend to have longer original papers compared to Psychology. The average length of original papers in Experimental Economics is 28 pages, whereas in Psychology, the average is 11 pages.
native_result.HypoB: In these replication-project data, original papers in Experimental Economics are substantially longer than those in Psychology: on average 28.0 pages (n = 18 papers, bootstrap 95% CI [24.8, 31.3]) versus 11.2 pages (n = 97 papers, CI [10.0, 12.4]) - a difference of 16.8 pages (CI [13.5, 20.4]) and a ratio of 2.5x (CI [2.1, 2.9]). The gap holds across the whole distribution (every ee paper exceeds the rpp median; P(ee > rpp) ~ 0.96) and is robust to lab-level vs study-level rows, excluding drop==True studies, and trimmed/winsorized means (11.0-12.0 pages for Psychology, 27.7-28.0 for Experimental Economics); alternative definitions of 'Psychology' barely change it (rpp+ml1+ml3 = 11.07, n = 123). This describes the original papers sampled by the Reproducibility Project: Psychology and the experimental-economics replication project in these data - not a general law about all publications in either field - and partly reflects publication conventions (ee papers are AER/QJE articles of 16-45 pages, while the rpp set includes 8 short 1-3 page reports), with limited precision for ee because n = 18.
native_result.WorkflowB: Loaded the study_data CSV (927x57); verified `length` (int64, 0 missing, range 1-45, constant within each `id`); deduplicated to study level by `id` (141 studies: ee 18, rpp 97, ml1 16, ml3 10); computed mean/median/SD/min-max per project with 2000-resample percentile bootstrap CIs (seed 20261022); bootstrapped the ee-rpp difference and ratio plus a two-sided bootstrap p, cross-checked with Welch t and Mann-Whitney U; reported alternative 'Psychology' definitions (rpp+ml1+ml3; discipline Social+Cognitive) as non-main; ran sensitivity controls (no dedup, drop==True exclusion, 5% trimmed, p95 winsorized, excluding 1-3 page papers); did not join the replication_success CSV (143x15, no length column, different EERP/SSRP study set).
